name: Otxandio – Andikona bombing memorial
story: On 22 July 1936, four days after the coup, two Breguet XIX light bombers flown from Recajo (La Rioja) by Ángel Salas Larrazábal and José Muñoz Jiménez bombed and machine-gunned the Andikona square in Otxandio. The square was crowded for the Santa Marina fiestas. About 61 people were killed, most of them civilians and many of them children. Otxandio sat on the front between Biscay and Álava. The raid is often called 'the first Gernika', because it was one of the first air attacks of the war to kill a crowd of civilians. A sculpture in the square honours the victims.
see: The village square (Andikona) with a memorial sculpture to the victims of the bombing.
plan: A small village on the BI-623 between Durango and Vitoria; the square is in the centre, so parking and a 20-minute visit are easy.

boxes.text: Deaths are recorded as 57–61; Paul Preston cites 84. There is debate over whether this or the 18 July raid on Tetuán was the war's first bombing.
